ver: Version counter. Starts at 1; incremented on every write.
meta.title: Application name, copied from PRD meta.title.
meta.updated_at: ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD) of the last write.
id: Screen ID matching the entry in screen-index, e.g. 'screen-001--login'.
name: Human-readable screen name, e.g. 'Login'.
module_id: Module ID this screen belongs to, matching module-index.
route: URL path or route for this screen — e.g. '/login', '/orders/:id'. Use naming conventions from shared-decisions. For non-web screens, use a descriptive identifier (e.g. 'OrderDetailView').
auth_requirement: Authentication requirement for this screen — e.g. 'public', 'authenticated', 'role: admin'. Derive from business spec actors and auth mechanism in shared-decisions.
actor_permissions: Access rules per actor for this screen. One entry per actor listed in the business spec.
actor_permissions[].can_access: true if this actor can access this screen; false otherwise.
actor_permissions[].conditions: Any additional conditions required for access — e.g. 'only if account is verified', 'only owns the resource'. Empty string if no additional conditions.
api_contracts: Technical contracts per use case on this screen. One entry per usecase_id in the business spec. For non-API systems, this is an empty array [].
api_contracts[].endpoints: List of API endpoints that implement this use case. Most use cases map to one endpoint; complex ones (e.g. list + create) may have multiple.
api_contracts[].endpoints[].path: API path — e.g. '/api/orders', '/api/orders/:id'. Must follow shared-decisions naming_conventions.
api_contracts[].endpoints[].description: One-line description of what this endpoint does.
api_contracts[].endpoints[].auth_require: true if this endpoint requires authentication.
api_contracts[].endpoints[].request.path: List of path parameter definitions. Each item: { name, type, description }. Empty array if none.
api_contracts[].endpoints[].request.quer: List of query parameter definitions. Each item: { name, type, required, default, description }. Empty array if none.
api_contracts[].endpoints[].request.body: Request body as a JSON object describing field names and types. Use {} if no body (e.g. GET). Derive from usecase main_flow input steps.
api_contracts[].endpoints[].response.suc: Success response body as a JSON object. Include pagination wrapper if applicable (per shared-decisions.pagination). Derive from screen information_displayed and usecase postconditions.
api_contracts[].endpoints[].response.err: List of error response objects for this endpoint. Each item: { http_code, error_code, condition }. Follow shared-decisions.error_format.
Caching strategy — e.g. 'No cache', 'Cache 5 min, invalidate on write'. Empty string if not applicable.
Rate limiting — e.g. 'No limit', '60 req/min per user'. Empty string if not applicable.
api_contracts[].business_logic: Step-by-step backend logic for this use case as an ordered list of strings. Derive from usecase main_flow. Include: validation → auth check → business checks → DB ops → side effects → return response. Use arrow notation for branching: '→ if [condition]: return [error]'.
api_contracts[].data_operations: Database or storage operations performed by this use case. One entry per distinct operation.
api_contracts[].data_operations[].entity: Entity ID from entity-catalog that is operated on.
api_contracts[].data_operations[].descri: What is being read or written, and any conditions — e.g. 'SELECT order by id WHERE owner = current user', 'INSERT new order with status=pending'.
api_contracts[].edge_case_handling: How specific edge cases from the business spec are handled technically. Derive from usecase alternative_flows and screen edge_cases.
api_contracts[].edge_case_handling[].con: The edge case or error condition — e.g. 'Email already registered', 'Item out of stock at checkout time'.
api_contracts[].edge_case_handling[].han: How it is handled in the implementation — e.g. 'Return 409 CONFLICT with code EMAIL_ALREADY_EXISTS', 'Return 422 ITEM_UNAVAILABLE with item_id in payload'.
api_contracts[].business_rules_applied: List of business rules (from business spec) that this use case enforces. Each entry is a plain-English statement of the rule as applied technically.
shared_entities: Entities used by more than one use case in this screen. Helps developers understand which data structures are central to this screen.
shared_entities[].operations: List of operation types performed on this entity across all use cases — e.g. ['SELECT', 'UPDATE'].
screen_dependencies: Other screens or external services this screen depends on at runtime. E.g. must be authenticated via login screen, reads data created by another screen.
screen_dependencies[].screen_id: Screen ID from screen-index, or a descriptive label for external services.
screen_dependencies[].reason: Why this screen depends on that screen or service.
implementation_notes: Implementation-specific notes for developers. Include: performance concerns, concurrency risks, external service calls, complex validations, security considerations, or anything not captured elsewhere. Empty array if none.
api_contracts[].unit_test_cases: Unit test cases for the service-layer logic of this use case. Derived automatically from business_logic branching and edge_case_handling.
api_contracts[].unit_test_cases[].descri: Short description of what this test case verifies, e.g. 'returns 401 when user not found'.
api_contracts[].unit_test_cases[].given: The mock/stub state before calling the service method, e.g. 'userRepo.findByEmail() returns null'.
api_contracts[].unit_test_cases[].expect: The expected return value or thrown exception, e.g. 'throw UnauthorizedException with code INVALID_CREDENTIALS'.
test_scenarios: Technical test bindings for all test layers, one entry per BDD scenario from Phase 2. Derived from Phase 2 bdd_scenarios + api_contracts.
test_scenarios[].scenario_ref: The Phase 2 bdd_scenarios.scenario name this entry maps to, e.g. 'User Login — success'.
test_scenarios[].usecase_id: The usecase ID this scenario belongs to.
test_scenarios[].api_test: Ordered list of API call steps for this scenario. One entry per API call; use multiple steps when the scenario requires sequential calls (e.g. POST /orders → POST /payments → GET /orders/:id).
test_scenarios[].api_test[].step: Step number starting at 1. Defines execution order.
test_scenarios[].api_test[].endpoint: HTTP method and path for this step.
test_scenarios[].api_test[].request_exam: Concrete request body or params for this step. May reference response fields from a previous step using {{stepN.field}} notation.
test_scenarios[].api_test[].expected_sta: Expected HTTP status code for this step, e.g. 200, 201, 401, 422.
test_scenarios[].api_test[].expected_err: Expected error_code string in the response body for this step, or null for success steps.
test_scenarios[].component_test: Component test binding — what to render, what to do, what to assert. Empty object if no frontend.
test_scenarios[].component_test.componen: Name of the UI component under test, e.g. 'LoginForm'.
test_scenarios[].component_test.action: User interaction to simulate, e.g. 'fill valid email and password, click submit'.
test_scenarios[].component_test.assert: What to assert after the action, e.g. 'loading state shown, redirect triggered'.
test_scenarios[].browser_test: Browser test binding — route, action, and assertion in a real browser. Empty object if no frontend.
test_scenarios[].browser_test.route: URL route to navigate to, copied from screen.route.
test_scenarios[].browser_test.action: Browser interaction steps, e.g. 'fill email and password, click Login button'.
test_scenarios[].browser_test.assert: What to assert in the browser after the action, e.g. 'redirected to /dashboard'.
